`self.font_shaper.shape(r)` makes a fresh `&mut` from the Renderer’s tag: a sibling of the hook. Its Unique function-entry retag pops everything above the Renderer’s tag, including <3065>.
`add_glyph_mut(&mut self)` reborrows the whole Renderer, which covers the Shaper bytes too. The hook was already gone.
Next `it.next()` re-derefs the hook: “trying to retag from <3065> … but that tag does not exist in the borrow stack”.

shape() writes `self.tick` through the sibling `&mut self.font_shaper`: a foreign write for <2954>, which becomes Disabled.
“reborrow through <2954> … is forbidden”: Disabled forbids even a child read.

commit.subject: rustty: xev loop core + Completion/Operation + tick (Send/Default discipline)

impl.note: Shown at dcae8d61e~1. The queue module itself warned against `&mut self`; its callers in the event loop still formed a fresh `&mut` at every site.

lines: … The queue is self-referential (`head`/`tail` point at the
// embedded `stub`), so all methods take a raw `*mut Self` (Zig `*Self`) to keep
// allocation-wide pointer provenance; a `&mut self` receiver would invalidate the
// stored stub pointer under Stacked Borrows.
/// The MPSC queue for completed completions from the thread pool.

review.head: A pointer-lifetime audit (two medium findings of 20) found it in a branch no test reached.

quotes.who: Audit finding — tick: retags invalidate the queue’s stub pointers
quotes.text: each `&mut self.thread_pool_completions` coerced to `*mut Self` is a fresh SB retag; the stub self-pointers written by init (line 630’s tag) are invalidated by line 740’s retag (and by each tick’s `&mut self`), making pop’s deref of the stored tail SB UB even single-threaded — contradicting queue_mpsc.rs’s own PORT NOTE (lines 14-17) and the rows’ stable-`*mut` prescription.

`thread_perform` runs on a pool thread and forms `&mut (*(*c).task_loop).thread_pool_completions` — a unique reference concurrent with the loop thread’s accesses (UB regardless of the AtomicPtr ops inside), whose retag also invalidates the stored stub self-pointers.
the prescribed one-line `addr_of_mut!((*self_ptr)...)` fix is NOT trivially provable […] Exactly the class of fix doctrine says must not be hand-reasoned.

sb.say: tick_naive(&mut self): the loop is reborrowed whole, protected for the call.
`&mut self.q` coerced to `*mut QPlain`: “<2681> was created by a SharedReadWrite retag” here.
init stores `head = tail = &stub`: pointers into the queue that carry tag <2681>.
The next `&mut self.q` is a new Unique retag from tick’s tag. It pops <2681>, the tag the stored stub pointers carry (the audit’s “line 630’s tag … invalidated by line 740’s retag”).
`head.swap` returns the old stub pointer, still tagged <2681>; `AtomicPtr::from_ptr(next_field(prev))` retags from it: “that tag does not exist in the borrow stack”.

tb.say: <2627> created by `&mut self.q`, initial state Reserved. The raw stub pointers inherit it.
`stub.next = null` is a child write: <2627> becomes Unique.
The second `&mut self.q` reborrow acts as a foreign read: <2627> becomes Frozen.
push stores `prev.next = v` through the old stub pointer (child <2666>): “Frozen which forbids this child write access”.
